Open Start and type your company name and your own limits in the yellow cells: warning days, the share over plan that turns amber or red, weeks in red before escalation, days allowed to send minutes and health score weights.
Fill Projects with each project: client, contact, manager, sponsor, dates and percent done. Health, weeks in red, open actions, decisions waiting and the next meeting fill in from the other sheets.

List your people on Team and your stakeholders on Stakeholder Register with influence and interest from 1 to 5 and the attitude. The quadrant and the strategy appear by themselves; set the days between contacts on Stakeholder Map.
Plan the engagement on Engagement Plan, and record every talk on Stakeholder Contacts. Days since contact and the overdue flag move on their own.
Set the rhythm of messages on Communication Plan and of reports on Report Calendar. The next date and the days to go are calculated.
Enter every meeting on Meetings and its minutes on Meeting Minutes. Cost of the meeting and the minutes check fill in; Upcoming Meetings and Attendance cover the next four weeks.
Write each action on Action Items with its owner and due date and mark it done on the day. Action Owners shows who is open, overdue and quick.
Every week enter one row per project on Weekly Status Reports: four ratings, percent done, achievements and next steps. Portfolio by Week counts green, amber and red.
Use Steering Pack Items and Sponsor Decisions to prepare the steering meeting: headline, decision needed, owner and how long each decision has waited.
Log client updates on Client Updates and client answers from 0 to 10 on Client Feedback. Reply days and follow-up checks are calculated.

Use the 14 calculators for meeting cost, status health, stakeholder strategy, channels, report due dates, action closure, attendance, health score, escalation, next meeting, satisfaction, steering counters and meeting load.

Run acceptance, testing, payments, handover and closure in one workbook
Acceptance, tests, defects, payments, handover and project closure
Acceptance log with days to decide
every submission shows its decision, the days the client took, the decision deadline and a flag for late or overdue acceptance
Deliverables with late and waiting checks
about 225 deliverables show days late against plan, submissions, days waiting and the payment each acceptance releases
each criterion is met, not met or not checked, so you know exactly what stands between a deliverable and its acceptance
Test cycles against your exit level
cases planned, run, passed and failed give the pass rate and a check against the exit level you set, with a flag for cycles not complete
Defect log with fix targets by severity
each defect shows its age, days to close, the fix target for its severity, reopen count and root cause, with a warning for late fixes
Root causes with prevention and rework cost
every analysed defect has a cause, the hours to fix, the rework cost from the fixer's rate and a prevention action you can tick off
Quality by month: rework and cost of quality
effort, rework, review and prevention hours per project and month give the rework share, defects found and closed, and a check against limits
each milestone is linked to a deliverable and shows the due date from the client terms, days late, amount outstanding and an invoice-to-send flag
items for the support team have owners, dates and status, and each service shows the share handed over and whether support can start
Benefits tracking against the planned level
actual against planned value month by month gives the achieved share of each benefit, a check against your limits and the next review date
Warranty periods with days left and claims
every warranty shows scope, days left, the share of the period used, the claims so far and a warning before it ends
Project health score with your weights
schedule, cost, quality, risk and client scores are weighted with the limits you set into one score and a green, amber or red colour per project

Projects: delivery, quality and health figures
One row per project with client, manager, dates, budget and percent done; deliverables accepted, pass rate, open defects, rework share and a health score from your weights fill in by themselves.
Team: roles, phones and open quality work
One row per team member with role, cost per hour, phone and e-mail; test cases run, defects assigned, reviews done, closure tasks and handover items open fill in by themselves.
Deliverables and milestones: dates, acceptance, days late
One row per deliverable or milestone with dates, owner, acceptor and status; submissions, days to accept, days late, the payment tied to it and a late or waiting check fill in.
Acceptance log: every submission and the client decision
One row per submission of a deliverable with reviewer, decision, comments and dates; days to decide, days waiting, the deadline, the phones and a check fill in by themselves.
Acceptance criteria: what the client checks
One row per criterion of a deliverable with who checked it and when; the deliverable name, the project and a met, not met or not checked state fill in by themselves.
Test cases: area, expected result and result
One row per key test case with area, expected result, result, tester and date; the defect logged for a failed case, the tester phone and a check for a failure without a defect fill in by themselves.
Test cycles: cases run, passed, failed and the exit level
One row per test cycle with cases planned, run and passed; failed cases, pass rate, coverage, the manager and tester phones and a check against your exit level fill in by themselves.
Defect log: severity, status, age and fix target
One row per defect with severity, status, finder, assignee and dates; open flag, age, days to close, the fix target for the severity, root cause and a late-fix check fill in.
Root causes: why a defect happened and how to prevent it
One row per analysed defect with the cause, the hours to fix and the prevention action; the project, severity, assignee, rework cost and a check for prevention not yet done fill in by themselves.
Quality reviews: documents, code, process and release checks
One row per quality review with subject, reviewer, hours, findings and score out of 100; the manager phone, findings per hour and a pass or follow-up check fill in by themselves.
Quality by month: effort, rework and review hours
One row per project and month with the effort, rework, review and prevention hours; rework share, the share spent on quality, defects found and closed in the month and a check fill in by themselves.
Payment milestones: the money released by each acceptance
One row per payment milestone of a client project, tied to a deliverable (internal projects have none); terms, due date, a check, days late and the amount outstanding fill in.
Handover items: runbook, access, training, contacts
One row per item handed to the client or the support team, with owner, due date and status; the owner and client phones, days left and a check for overdue or blocked items fill in by themselves.
Support transition: who supports each service
One row per service moving to support with the support owner, phone and start date; the share of handover items done, days to start and a readiness check fill in from the handover items.
Benefits register: what each project should deliver
One row per benefit with measure, baseline, target, go-live date, owner and review date; the last month, actual, achieved share against plan and a check fill in from Benefits Tracking.
Benefits tracking: actual against plan by month
One row per benefit and month with the actual value and the planned level; the achieved share, the project, the measure and a check against your on-target limit fill in by themselves.
Closure tasks: what must be done to close a project
One row per closure task with owner, due date and done date; the owner and manager phones, days late and a check for overdue or due-soon tasks fill in by themselves.
Post-project reviews: ratings and main lessons

One row per respondent of a post-project review with ratings from 1 to 5 for schedule, cost, scope and client, and the main lesson; the overall rating, the PMO phone and a check fill in by themselves.
Acceptance certificates: signed proof of acceptance
One row per acceptance certificate with version, date and signer; the deliverable name, the client phone, days since signing and a check for a missing signed copy fill in by themselves.
Warranty periods: scope, end date and claims
One row per warranty period with scope, start, end and claims; the days left, the share of the period used, the client and manager phones and a check for periods ending soon fill in by themselves.

Hello {contact}, deliverable {name} of {project} is submitted for acceptance. Please check it against the agreed criteria and tell us your decision.
Client contact: please accept or comment
Hello {contact}, please accept deliverable {name} or send your comments by {decide_by}. If something is unclear, call me and we will go through it together.
Hello {contact}, deliverable {name} has been waiting {waiting} days for your decision. Please accept it or send your comments this week.
Hello {contact}, thank you for accepting deliverable {name} on {decided_on}. We will invoice the milestone linked to it.
Client contact: returned, plan to fix
Hello {contact}, thank you for the review of {name}. Your comments: {comments}. We will send a fix plan with dates within two working days.
Hello {contact}, we hold {name} for {project} on {planned}. Please confirm who will attend and tell us about any open concern before then.
Hello {contact}, the handover session on {item} for {project} is planned for {due}. Please confirm who attends from {to_whom}.
Hello {contact}, the warranty of {project} ends on {end}. Please send any claim before then so that we can solve it in time.
Hello {contact}, the benefits review for {project} is on {review}, in about {months_left} months. Please keep the latest figures for {benefit} ready.
Hello {contact}, {name} is complete. We invite you to a short review of what worked and what we should do better. Please tell us a time that suits you.
Hello {contact}, the final acceptance letter for {name} is ready: {accepted} of {deliverables} deliverables are accepted. Please sign and return it.
Team member: defect assigned to you
Hello, defect {defect_id} "{title}" ({severity}) on {project} is assigned to you. The fix target is {target} days. Please start and tell me the fix date.
Hello, defect {defect_id} "{title}" on {project} is fixed. Please retest it and close it or send it back with a note.
Team member: critical defect, fix today
Hello, critical defect {defect_id} "{title}" on {project} has been open {age} days. Please fix it today and tell me when it is ready to retest.
Hello {tester}, test cycle {cycle_id} ({cycle}, round {round}) on {project} starts on {date}. Please prepare {planned} cases and the test data.
Team member: closure task is due
Hello {owner}, closure task "{task}" on {project} is due on {due}. Please finish it and tell me when it is done.
Hello {manager}, defect {defect_id} "{title}" on {project} is {age} days old and the target is {target} days. Please decide who helps to close it.
Project manager: pass rate too low
Hello {manager}, test cycle {cycle_id} on {project} has a pass rate of {pass_rate}, below the exit level. {failed} cases failed. Please agree the fix plan with the team.
Hello, deliverable {name} on {project} has waited {waiting} days for the client. The decision was due by {decide_by}. Please call {contact}.
Hello, closure task "{task}" on {project} is owned by {owner} and is due on {due}. It is {days_late} days late if it shows a number. Please check it.
Hello {sponsor}, health of {name}: score {health} ({health_state}), {delay} days behind plan, test pass rate {pass_rate}, {crit_open} critical defects open. Please review it before sign-off.
Hello {sponsor}, benefit "{benefit}" of {project} is at {achieved} of the planned level. The next review is on {review}. Please look at the actions needed.
Hello {support_owner}, the handover pack for {service} on {project} is ready. Support starts on {start}. Please confirm that you received it.

Hello {support_owner}, I am sending the access and contacts list for {service} on {project}. Please check your accounts before {start}. Handover items done: {handover_done}.
Hello, milestone {milestone} on {project} was accepted on {accepted_on}. Please invoice {amount} to {contact}. The client terms are {terms} days.

Track each warranty on Warranty Periods: days left, the share of the period used and a warning before it ends.
